title: Shallow approximation of decision trees
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\alpha$ be a type with decidable equality, and let $T$ be a binary decision tree whose queries use coordinates from a fixed subset of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For any fallback label in $\alpha$ and any real $\varepsilon>0$, there is a tree $T'$ on the same available coordinates whose depth is at most $\left\lceil\log_2\bigl(\operatorname{leafCount}(T)/\varepsilon\bigr)\right\rceil$, and whose outputs disagree with those of $T$ on at most an $\varepsilon$ fraction of inputs in $\{0,1\}^n$.
hypotheses_covered: Tree $T$ over a fixed available subset of the $n$ coordinates
